To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phytic acid can be reduced by 76 % and fiber increased by 10 % in wheat bran by applying particle size reduction, wet steeping in buffer and fermentation.
particle size reduction, fermentation and hydrothermal treatments decreased phytic acid content, while hydrothermal treatment increased fiber content.
particle size reduction, fermentation and hydrothermal treatment reduced the phytic acid content in wheat bran.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reduction of phytic acid content in bran and the improvement of some physicochemical and nutritional properties.
the reduction of phytic acid content, which may have positive effect on the nutritional value of bran.
a new method of reducing phytic acids and improving some functional properties of the bran by combining particle size reduction and hydrothermal and/or fermentation treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
particle size reduction and hydrothermal treatments are the most effective methods in reducing phytic acid and increasing dietary fiber content of wheat bran.
particle size reduction along with hydrothermal treatment would be a promising approach to reduce phytic acid content in bran with minimum loss of fiber.
the combination of hydrothermal and particle size reduction treatments resulted in the highest fiber content and the lowest phytic content of the bran.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
particle size reduction, especially along with hydrothermal and/or fermentation treatments, could be applied as a pre-treatment to improve the nutritional value and functional properties of bran.

particle size reduction, fermentation and hydrothermal treatments reduced phytic acid in bran, while particle size alone and in combination with hydrothermal or fermentation treatments increased fiber content.

hydrothermal treatment and particle size reduction are effective treatments for reducing phytic acid, but particle size reduction is more effective than hydrothermal treatment in increasing fiber content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hydrothermal treatment along particle size reduction could be used to reduce phytic acid content in wheat bran.
particle size reduction, fermentation and hydrothermal treatments can reduce phytic acid content in bran.
the combination of hydrothermal treatment with particle size reduction could be a good strategy for reducing the phytic acid content while maintaining high fiber content of wheat bran.
